inspection_outcome: One confirmed Major parameter obstruction in the optimal higher-differentiability proof and six Minor comments with precise normalized-use limitations. No principal theorem counterexample claimed.

findings.location: p.42 equation (4.21), reused pp.44-45 in Lemma4.6; downstream pp.47-48
findings.claim: For all 0<sigma<2s0-1 there exists beta in (0,1) with 2s0 beta-1>(sigma+1)/2>sigma.
findings.hypotheses: n=2,s=s0=3/5,sigma=1/10,Phi(t)=t,Lambda=1,u=0,mu=0,R=1 satisfy Lemma4.6 assumptions. This tests parameter existence, not failure of the zero solution.
findings.decisive_evidence: sup over beta<1 of 2s0 beta-1=1/5 <11/20; required beta>31/24. General feasibility needs sigma<4s0-3.
findings.impact: The claimed optimal differentiability proof cannot start on a substantial admitted range. Lemma4.6 feeds Theorem1.9 and Corollary5.2, then the potential-estimate chain. Homogeneous Theorem1.5 does not use it.
findings.repair_boundary: Explicit a,beta,K,T and capped recurrence in the report repair the exponent arithmetic with strict margins. Numerical example first crosses target at step18. All analytic covering/tail/localization constants must still be rewritten; no completed replacement theorem proof or conclusion counterexample.

findings.claim: The formal PV operator, displayed energy, and weak form use the same normalization.
findings.hypotheses: Phi(t)=t, nonconstant u=psi smooth compact support, any n>=2,0<s<1; mu=(formal Lu)dx finite with locally bounded and integrable-tail density.
findings.decisive_evidence: The printed bilinear form equals 2 integral(formal Lu*psi); positive energy for u=psi rules out equality with factor1.
findings.impact: Formal normalization mismatch; subsequent estimates use unspecified constants and the weak form consistently.
findings.repair_boundary: Double the formal operator prefactor, or halve the energy and weak-form integral prefactors. Does not refute qualitative estimates.

findings.claim: An averaged Sobolev norm is bounded by the unnormalized seminorm with c(n,gamma,q), no R factor.
findings.hypotheses: n=2,q=2,gamma=1/2, g_R=x1/R on B_R; n>q gamma and finite seminorm.
findings.decisive_evidence: LHS=8^(-1/4); RHS seminorm=R^(1/2) times fixed positive constant. R down to0 refutes the bound.
findings.impact: False unrestricted-radius lemma display. The p.40 use is normalized to radii in [1/4,1/2], where the missing factor is bounded.
findings.repair_boundary: Insert R^(gamma-n/q). This normalized downstream application remains compatible with the corrected inequality.

findings.claim: At h=2s-1 the normalized comparison seminorm has RHS R^(-s/2+2s-n) times measure mass.
findings.hypotheses: n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,u_R=R^(2s) phi(x/R) with nonzero C_c^infty(B_1/2) bump; v_R=0 since exterior values vanish; mu_R is its weak-form forcing, bounded in B_R.
findings.decisive_evidence: LHS=R*A with A>0; RHS=cR^(9/8)*M with M>0, because |mu_R|(B_R)=R^n M. Ratio diverges as R down to0. KMS Lemma3.2 has r^(-h)r^(2s-n), giving r^(1-n).
findings.impact: False non-unit-radius intermediate estimate. Later R=1 uses and the final correctly scaled L1 comparison are not refuted.
findings.repair_boundary: Use R^(1-n) at h=2s-1 and the corresponding Poincare factor. Uniform s-dependence still requires tracking the external estimates; the displayed prefactor simplifies exactly to4.

findings.claim: The inhomogeneous difference-quotient Holder estimate has no R^(2s) multiplying its data term.
findings.hypotheses: n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,beta=1,h=e1; phi smooth supported B1 and equal x1 on B1/2; w_L=L phi(x/L),R=L^2,L>3; f_L is the weak-form forcing. All energy/tail/bounded-forcing hypotheses and h<R/8 hold.
findings.decisive_evidence: delta_h w_L(0)=1; average term<=C L^(-n), tail=0, and ||delta_h f_L||infty<=C L^(-2s). Printed RHS tends0.
findings.impact: False radius-uniform statement, but the actual nonhomogeneous bootstrap applies it on R=1 and the other relevant use has f=0.
findings.repair_boundary: Restore R^(2s) as in Lemma2.13. Linear test homogeneity is used only for the counterexample, not asserted for general Phi.

findings.claim: Truncated-to-classical Riesz comparison has c(n) for arbitrary beta in (0,n).
findings.hypotheses: n=2, beta=2-epsilon with0<epsilon<1, unit Dirac measure at e1,x0=0,R=exp(1/epsilon).
findings.decisive_evidence: Classical potential1; truncated potential=(1-exp(-1))/epsilon, unbounded as epsilon down to0.
findings.impact: Overly general uniformity assertion. Actual beta=2s-1<1 applications with n>=2 have n-beta>1 and are unaffected.
findings.repair_boundary: Include factor1/(n-beta) or explicitly restrict beta to the applied range.

findings.location: p.19 displayed Lemma2.8 application after (2.15); p.20 Lemma2.10 proof
findings.claim: A qth-power estimate is bounded by a qth root, and first differences divided by |h|^(1+gamma) have a finite global supremum.
findings.hypotheses: For p.19 q=2, smooth cutoff H=G xi from g=x1^2 and arbitrary positive amplitude; all seminorms finite. For p.20 n=2,R=1,h0=1/10,gamma=1/2,g=x1 on required ball, with xi=1 on B21/20; (2.16) holds.
findings.decisive_evidence: Amplitude scaling gives A^2 on left versus A on right. At p.20, for h=t e1 the first-difference integral>=pi*t^(-1/2) diverges.
findings.impact: Two false intermediate displays; preceding product calculation and subsequent M^q bound support the local corrections, rather than a refutation of the embedding conclusions.
findings.repair_boundary: Remove the qth root after taking qth powers; replace delta_h(g xi) by delta_h^2(g xi).

observations_requiring_clarification: For Proposition5.4 keep the outermost measure term or start one scale inward/enlarge potential radius. A shell near R disproves the measure-only comparison of |mu|(B_R)/R^(n-beta) to I_beta(x,R); no counterexample to Proposition5.4 itself is asserted.
Pass SOLA limits in finite-scale ball-mass sums at continuity radii before the number of scales tends to infinity; weak measure convergence alone is not a dominating function for full potentials.
Secant kernel for u-v, rather than identifying the individual kernels K_u and K_v, supplies the correct comparison route.
Free bootstrap exponents can be reduced to avoid beta+gamma=1 or an infinite Sobolev conjugate; this does not fix the fixed-parameter obstruction P1.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: Lemma 4.6 allows n=2, Phi(t)=t, Lambda=1, s=s0=3/5, sigma=1/10, u=0, mu=0 and R=1. The existential beta must lie strictly in (0,1) for every admitted sigma.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: 2s0 beta-1 has supremum 1/5 but must exceed (sigma+1)/2=11/20, requiring beta>31/24. Generally feasibility requires sigma<4s0-3, which is stricter than sigma<2s0-1 and empty for positive sigma when s0<=3/4.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: Zero u is not a regularity counterexample. Actual pp.44-45 use the unavailable exponent in the iteration; pp.47-48 invoke Lemma 4.6 in Theorem 1.9 and Corollary 5.2. The homogeneous Theorem 1.5 is separate.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: With a=(sigma+2s0-1)/2 and beta=(1+(a+1)/(2s0))/2, sigma<a<2s0 beta-1 and beta<1. T=s0(1+sigma)/2 exceeds sigma by (1-s0)^2+(2-s0)(2s0-1-sigma)/2. b_(j+1)=min(a,beta b_j+T(1-beta)) crosses sigma finitely; the recorded exact example crosses at 18. This only fixes exponent arithmetic, not the complete analytic proof.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: The exact formal operator (1.2), energy (1.4), odd Phi assumption and weak double-integral form (1.15) were viewed.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: Swap x,y in the double integral and use oddness: the weak bilinear integral is twice the formal PV pairing. For Phi identity and nonconstant smooth compact u=psi, its energy is positive. The induced formal forcing is locally bounded with integrable tail, hence is an admissible finite signed measure.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: This is a formal normalization conflict. Estimates expressed with unspecified constants and consistent use of the weak operator do not become false from that factor alone.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Double the formal operator prefactor or halve the energy and weak-form prefactors; do not relabel this a counterexample to the qualitative regularity conclusions.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: p.13 distinguishes ordinary and averaged integrals. p.14 defines the unnormalized fractional seminorm and states Lemma 2.3 with c(n,gamma,q) independent of arbitrary R. n=2,q=2,gamma=1/2 satisfy n>q gamma.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: For g_R=x1/R on B_R, mean zero, the averaged L4 norm equals (1/8)^(1/4), while the unnormalized seminorm equals R^(1/2) times a fixed positive finite constant. Let R decrease to zero.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: p.40 explicitly normalizes the later use to R=1 and subradii in [1/4,1/2]; the missing factor is bounded there.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Insert R^(gamma-n/q). The false all-radius display does not by itself invalidate the normalized downstream proof.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: p.35 has h=2s-1 and the printed measure coefficient R^(-s/2+2s-n). Choose n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,u_R=R^(2s)phi(x/R), smooth nonzero phi supported in B_(1/2); v_R=0 meets the zero exterior comparison data.
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: The weak forcing is F(x/R), so its B_R mass is R^n M, M>0 by the positive energy pairing. The normalized h-seminorm scales as R A, A>0, but the printed RHS scales as c R^(9/8) M. Their ratio diverges as R decreases to zero.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: The direct scaling contradiction is independent of external theorem validity. The normalized R=1 application and the distinct final R^(2s-n) L1 comparison are not refuted.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: R^(1-n) is the dimensionally correct coefficient at h=2s-1; the reported s-prefactor is exactly 4. Full uniform constants from the external estimate are not newly re-proved.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: Actually viewed Lemma 3.6 permits beta=1 and arbitrary R with c(n,s0,Lambda), while Lemma 2.13 includes R^(2s) F. Fix n=2,s=3/4,Phi identity,h=e1 and phi smooth compact in B1 equal to x1 on B_(1/2).
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: For w_L=L phi(x/L), R=L^2, L>3, delta_h w_L(0)=1, the normalized mean is O(L^(-n)), its tail beyond B_R is zero, and the forcing difference norm is O(L^(-2s)); all energy, tail, bounded-forcing and h<R/8 assumptions hold. The printed RHS tends to zero.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: The homogeneous proof viewed on pp.33-34 has zero forcing and the inhomogeneous normalized use has R=1.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Restore R^(2s) on the forcing term. Linear homogeneity is used only for this admissible counterfamily, not asserted for arbitrary nonlinear Phi.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: Viewed p.8: beta ranges over (0,n), both Riesz definitions are unnormalized as reported, and (1.19) claims c(n).
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: For n=2, beta=2-epsilon, unit mass at e1, x0=0, R=exp(1/epsilon), the classical potential is 1 whereas the truncated potential is (1-exp(-1))/epsilon, unbounded.
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: The later actual application is beta=2s-1<1 with n>=2, so 1/(n-beta) is bounded there.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Include 1/(n-beta) or state the restricted range; do not promote this broader uniformity error to a failure of the applied gradient estimates.

problem_reviews.definition_hypotheses_quantifiers: Viewed pp.18-20: Lemma 2.8's rooted norm, Lemma 2.9's q range and cutoff construction, and Lemma 2.10's first- and second-difference hypothesis (2.16).
problem_reviews.independent_decisive_reason: On p.19 the q-power left side scales as A^q under multiplication of g by A, but the displayed 1/q-root right side scales as A; q=2 and a nonzero smooth compact G xi contradict the line for large A. On p.20 choose n=2,R=1,h0=1/10,gamma=1/2,g=x1 on the required ball. (2.16) has finite M, but for h=t e1 the printed first-difference global integral is at least pi*t^(-1/2).
problem_reviews.counterevidence_and_dependency: The preceding second-difference product expansion and subsequent M^q bound support typographical local corrections; no embedding conclusion counterexample is established.
problem_reviews.repair_boundary: Remove the stray qth root on p.19 after taking qth powers, and use delta_h^2(g xi) on p.20.

independent_acceptance.decision_explanation: All seven reported Problems are supported as stated. Retain one Major proof-parameter obstruction and six Minor local normalization/scaling/display issues. The main theorem conclusions are not refuted. The proposed exponent repair is arithmetic only; analytic covering, tails and localization constants are not certified as a replacement proof. Current report TeX/PDF require no scientific revision.
